fixes.explanation: Nobody is checking Jacob's clock here, baker. Laban's sons are counting wealth, not hours, and they say he “built all this wealth at our father’s expense.” (Genesis 31:1) Jacob tells a different story, that he served their father “with all my strength.” (Genesis 31:6) So he worked hard and still got talked about.

Mama's not in this conversation, friend. Jacob says, “…the God of my father has been with me.” (Genesis 31:5) Rebekah is Jacob's mother (Genesis 28:5), but he's pointing Rachel and Leah to God. When the news is bad, he leads with the One who's been there the whole time.

Esau's name never comes up in this talk, baker. Jacob tells Rachel and Leah, “…the God of my father has been with me.” (Genesis 31:5) Esau is Jacob's brother (Genesis 27:11), but the One at Jacob's side out in that field is God. That credit goes to Him.

Fields? Not this time, friend. Jacob says, “Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.” (Genesis 31:9) It's the animals that changed hands, so the land stays out of it. Jacob did call his wives out to a field (Genesis 31:4), but that's just where they were standing.

Wrong column, friend. The angel says, “for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.” (Genesis 31:12) His eyes are on what Laban did, not on anything Jacob handed over. Jacob hears that nothing Laban did got missed.

Seir is a fun guess, but it's not on this map, baker. The text says Jacob is going “…to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.” (Genesis 31:18) Esau, Jacob's brother (Genesis 27:11), doesn't show up in this passage. Jacob's destination is Dad's place, and he's herding a whole crowd of animals there.

A cover story would have been a whole production, friend, and the text doesn't give one. It says Jacob deceived Laban “…by not telling him that he was running away.” (Genesis 31:20) No line about moving the flocks, no explanation at all. The deceiving was in what he kept back.
